correctness.rationale: Addition theorem yields exact sample Gram with factor (2ell+1)/12. Parity compression doubles it to (2ell+1)/6. The six axes form a tight frame, so C^2=5I; rank-one J and 3+3 Seidel eigenspaces give all singular values. Bernstein inequality excludes further odd exceptional degrees beyond 3 and even beyond 16, and an exact Legendre recurrence checks every remaining degree. Numerical tests independently assemble spherical harmonic evaluations through degree 25 but the proof does not rely on finite experiments. Full-domain quantifiers, factor conventions, and rank-six output limitation are explicit.

originality.rationale: The 2013 harmonic-index paper explicitly covers cancellations at degrees 8 and 14, and the icosahedral five-design covers 2 and 4; neither is claimed new. Full-text inspections of arXiv:1308.5101, arXiv:1403.4661 and relevant Section 4.2 of arXiv:1701.06617 find no theorem giving the complete normalized per-degree singular spectrum, all-degree zero-eigenvalue exhaustion and exact least-norm interpolation costs. The new combination is a full spectral theorem not a restatement of known design strength. An inaccessible icosahedral-representation paper and incomplete indexing leave residual priority risk.
residual_risks: Older symmetry-adapted icosahedral harmonic representation papers may contain an equivalent sampling eigenvalue decomposition; Zheng–Doerschuk and Cohan full text were unavailable.
The new formulas follow from the classical addition theorem and icosahedral association algebra, so independent priority review is necessary before publication.

value.rationale: Fixed-degree sampling on the minimal symmetric icosahedral mesh naturally asks when all six parity-compatible observations are attainable and how stable least-norm interpolation is. The theorem gives the complete nonzero-capable singular spectrum, exact intrinsic conditioning at each degree, a sharp final exceptional degree 14, and asymptotic approach to tight six-channel sampling. The earlier degree 8/14 design examples provide motivation but do not give this quantitative theorem. This is a structural measurement classification, not an arbitrary numerical invariant.
